overview: TargetStrafe turns the Aura target into an orbit center. The MoveEvent handler rebuilds the movement vector every tick from the aim yaw: RotationUtils.getRotations returns the bearing to the target, setSpeed applies a direction constant (consts, flipped by horizontal collision or a void probe) and a range-keeping correction, and the resulting x/z deltas are written straight into the event. The module activates only while Aura is on, a target is locked, the player is not sneaking, and one of Speed, Fly, Flight or LastestHypixelSpeed is running, so the orbit rides whatever speed the paired movement module produces. TargetStrafe constructs no packets itself: the event deltas flow into the C03 stream, and sprint C0B traffic appears because the orbit keymode keeps the player moving and jumping.

sections.p: setSpeed starts from the aim yaw returned by RotationUtils.getRotations(target, OtPosValue) and composes the motion direction as yaw plus 90 degrees plus strafe2, with the yaw pre-rotated by plus or minus cansize (45 in TrueRadius mode, 45 divided by the target distance in Simple mode) when KeepRange is on. strafe2 is plus or minus 45 divided by algorithm, where algorithm is max(Enemydistance - radius, Enemydistance - 0.5). The combined offset from the aim direction is 45 - 45/algorithm degrees, sweeping from near 0 at distance to 45 when the player hugs the exact orbit radius, so mid-orbit divergence from the reported look sits in the 10-40 degree band at sane radii and only the near-0 and near-45 instants align with the 45-degree grid.

The consts constant cycles through the check() routine: a horizontal collision or a void probe (isVoid scans the column under the player, exempt while Fly is on, treating posY below 0 as void) advances the counter, and the 0 -> 1 -> -1 cycle flips the orbit direction. With Radiusturn set to Player, the strafe component is multiplied by mc.thePlayer.movementInput.moveStrafe so the player steers the circle; with None it is purely the consts sign. KeepRange lifts the aim point by OtPos and the radius modes change cansize only. The Render3D handler draws the orbit cylinder (TScylinder rings at radius plus or minus 0.013) and forces thirdPersonView to 4 while strafing; both are render-side and never touch the wire.

The module never calls a packet constructor; setSpeed writes moveEvent.x and moveEvent.z, and the fork's movement pipeline folds those deltas into the next C03 position, while the reported look stays with Aura's rotation, which converges on the same aim bearing. The gate requires a speed-capable module to be on, so the server sees the orbit as that module's movement with a continuously changing direction, and the sprint C0B stream appears because the keymode (jump key held plus movement input) keeps the player sprinting through the orbit. Envelope checks therefore measure the paired module's rate, while direction checks see the orbit's signature.

files.label: TargetStrafe.kt
files.explanation: The entire module: the canStrafe gate over Aura plus the speed-capable modules, the setSpeed orbit math, the consts direction cycle, the void probe, the Render3D cylinder drawing, and the third-person view forcing. It writes only MoveEvent deltas, so the C03 chip in the brief is the movement stream the deltas ride and the C0B chip is the sprint traffic of the moving player.

files.label: Events.kt (MoveEvent delta carrier)
files.explanation: MoveEvent (line 102) is the cancellable carrier whose x/y/z fields the fork's movement code reads when it builds the C03 position; TargetStrafe's setSpeed writes exactly those fields. The same file declares UpdateEvent and MotionEvent, the tick hooks the sibling modules use, and because the snapshot ships no net/minecraft tree, this event class is the verifiable bridge between the orbit math and the wire.

countering.label: Strafe (45-degree grid test)
countering.explanation: The check builds accelDir from the move delta minus the predicted velocity, measures the angle against the reported yaw, and accepts only angles within yawErrorThreshold (default 0.5 degrees) of the 45-degree grid. The orbit's 45 - 45/algorithm offset sweeps through the mid-grid band for most of the circle, so mid-orbit ticks flag and only the near-0 and near-45 instants pass; jump ticks and horizontal-collision ticks are skipped, which coincides with the module's own direction flips.

countering.label: SprintDirection (62-degree threshold miss)
countering.explanation: SprintDirection requires the server sprint state and flags only when the angle between the motion force and the yaw exceeds pi/4 + 0.3, about 62 degrees. The orbit divergence stays at or under 45 degrees at sane radii, so the check never engages: it is the honest miss in this set, and naming it as such matters because a generic sprint-motion check list would wrongly include it.

countering.label: SurvivalFly (movement envelope)
countering.explanation: The module only runs with a speed-capable module enabled, and setSpeed multiplies the paired module's moveSpeed (lastDist) into the orbit direction, so the server sees the orbit as that module's output with a changing heading. SurvivalFly's horizontal allowance and rate ceiling set the player back once the combination exceeds vanilla acceleration, which is the over-speed envelope the orbit inherits rather than creates.

countering.label: Speed (distance accumulator)
countering.explanation: Arc v2's Speed measures distance, not direction: on ground it compares thisMove against thisMove divided by groundTime plus baseMove once groundTicks reaches 5, and off ground against the stage model. The orbit adds no distance over the paired module's output, so this check only bites when that module over-accelerates; the orbit's own signature is directional, which is Hawk Strafe's domain, so the two checks divide the surface cleanly.
